title: Great Wall of Qi, Shandong
summary: The Great Wall of Qi, in modern Shandong, is reported to be the earliest and longest of China's early long walls, about 641 km. A 2024 excavation at Guangli village, Changqing, Jinan, found several building phases from the late Western Zhou or early Spring and Autumn period to the Warring States.

uncertainty.note: Earliest phase late Western Zhou (1046-771 BCE) to early Spring and Autumn (770-476 BCE); the final phase is attributed to King Xuan of Qi (c. 350-301 BCE) by Discover. Range is the span of phases, not one construction date.

where.modern_name: Changqing District, Jinan, Shandong, China (excavation at Guangli village); the wall runs about 641 km east to the Qingdao coast
where.historical_name: State of Qi, Zhou states, Eastern Zhou

importance.justification: Possibly the earliest long defensive wall in China, predating the Qin and Han walls by centuries.

reviewer_note: Dating rests on press reports of the Shandong Provincial Institute of Cultural Relics and Archaeology; no peer-reviewed report was found. Wall length and early phase widths vary between outlets. The id says 500 BCE; the range follows the sources. Pin is Changqing District, not the exact dig.
